target_user.role: Aerospace Fleet Reliability Engineer & Maintenance Operations Manager
target_user.organization: Commercial & Defense Aviation Operators / MRO Facilities
target_user.primary_objective: Proactively detect sub-component gas-turbine degradation, forecast Remaining Useful Life (RUL) with high precision, and schedule shop-level maintenance before unscheduled engine removals (UER) or in-flight shutdowns (IFSD).

problem_formulation.domain: Turbofan Engine Predictive Maintenance & Aerothermal Prognostics
problem_formulation.challenge: Aero-engines operate under harsh cyclic thermal and mechanical stresses. Traditional threshold alerts trigger too late, risking catastrophic failure, while scheduled time-based maintenance leads to premature, costly overhaul of healthy components. A multimodal temporal intelligence model must reason over multivariate continuous sensor waveforms to provide both an accurate scalar RUL forecast and natural language engineering rationales.
target_capabilities: Continuous multi-sensor temporal drift monitoring across flight cycles.
Physically grounded thermodynamic degradation detection (HPC stall margin erosion).
Zero-leakage split partitioning by physical engine asset ID.
Actionable shop-level maintenance prescriptions based on wear severity.

candidate_evaluations.name: NASA C-MAPSS Turbofan Degradation (FD001)
candidate_evaluations.provider: NASA Ames Prognostics Center of Excellence (PCoE)
candidate_evaluations.suitability_rationale: Optimal baseline benchmark: single operating regime eliminates confounding ambient temperature/altitude effects, isolating pure thermodynamic degradation dynamics. Extensively benchmarked across academic literature with established scoring functions.

candidate_evaluations.name: NASA C-MAPSS Turbofan Degradation (FD002)
candidate_evaluations.suitability_rationale: Strong candidate for regime generalization, but requires complex flight envelope normalization that obscures core temporal reasoning in initial benchmark baseline.

candidate_evaluations.name: NASA N-CMAPSS Commercial Aircraft Telemetry
candidate_evaluations.suitability_rationale: Higher fidelity sub-second sampling and full flight profiles, but heavy storage (~50GB) and lower engine population (15 units) constrain rapid agile training loops.

candidate_evaluations.name: PHM08 Prognostics Data Challenge
candidate_evaluations.suitability_rationale: Derivative of C-MAPSS with masked ground-truth test labels, making offline evaluation transparency and verifiable held-out scoring less reproducible.
